findings.observation: Reviewed the Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 6), Engineer's Summary Letter, all general notes sheets (Sheets 5, 6, 16), and searched site plan documents for any references to tower cranes. No tower crane is mentioned in any application form, engineering letter, construction notes, or plan sheet. No tower crane symbols, notes, or License Agreement applications for tower cranes were found in the submittal.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-01 requires a License Agreement for tower cranes if one is proposed. The condition 'If tower crane proposed' is not met for this project. No evidence exists in the submittal that a tower crane will be used. Therefore, this checklist item is not applicable to this site plan.
findings.explanation: No tower crane proposed for this project.

findings.observation: Searched the entire project directory for references to retention systems, excavation support, shoring, or temporary construction support systems in the ROW. Reviewed general construction notes (Sheet 5), utility plans (Sheet 18), and supplementary documents. Found references to 'retention' only in the context of stormwater retention ponds on private property, not retention/excavation support systems in the public right-of-way. No License Agreement application for retention or excavation support was found.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-02 applies only 'If retention/excavation support in ROW' is proposed. The submittal contains no evidence of retention or excavation support systems proposed in the public right-of-way. All construction appears to be within the property limits or involves standard utility trenching with conventional backfill methods. The condition triggering this requirement is not met.
findings.explanation: No retention or excavation support systems proposed in the ROW.

findings.observation: Used vision tool to analyze Sheets 14 and 15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plans) to identify whether awnings, canopies, benches, bike racks, or trash receptacles are shown in the public right-of-way. Vision analysis confirmed: bike racks (Key Note 1) are located entirely on private property inside the property line; building overhangs (Key Note 11) are contained within property boundaries and do not extend into ROW; no benches, trash receptacles, awnings, or canopies are shown in the ROW areas between property lines and street pavement along Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, or S. Lamar Blvd.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-03 applies 'If streetscape elements in ROW' are proposed. The vision analysis of the site plans confirms that all streetscape elements (bike racks, overhangs) are located on private property, not in the public right-of-way. No awnings, canopies, benches, or trash receptacles are proposed. Since no streetscape elements are proposed in the ROW, the triggering condition is not met.
findings.explanation: No streetscape elements (awnings, canopies, benches, bike racks, trash receptacles) shown in the ROW.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheets 14 and 15 confirmed a '5' PLANTING ZONE' is explicitly shown in the public right-of-way along Collier Street, located between the proposed curb and gutter and the property line. This planting zone contains circular symbols representing proposed street trees. Reviewed the Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 6, page 4) which asks 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project?' and is marked 'No'. Searched all supplementary documents and found no License Agreement application for street trees, landscaping, or irrigation in ROW. Searched site plan notes on Sheets 5, 6, 14, 15, and landscape sheets 42, 50, 51 for any License Agreement references and found none.
findings.reasoning: The triggering condition 'If street trees/landscaping/irrigation in ROW' is clearly met—the plans explicitly show a planting zone with street trees in the Collier Street ROW. However, no License Agreement application has been submitted, and the Consolidated Site Plan Application explicitly states that no License Agreement will be submitted. The checklist item describes the deficiency as 'License Agreement for street trees, landscaping, or irrigation in ROW not submitted or referenced.' This deficiency is present. Per the grouping overview, License Agreements must be 'approved or submitted prior to formal site plan approval.' The absence of this required agreement is a completeness deficiency.
findings.explanation: Planting zone with street trees shown in ROW along Collier Street, but no License Agreement application submitted or referenced on plans.
findings.resolution: Submit License Agreement application for street trees and landscaping proposed in the Collier Street right-of-way, or reference approved License Agreement on the site plan.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheets 14 and 15 (site plans showing ROW areas) confirmed no outdoor dining areas, seating, tables, chairs, or related features are shown in the public right-of-way along any street frontage (Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, S. Lamar Blvd). Reviewed hardscape plan (Sheet 46) and found no outdoor dining symbols or callouts. Searched project documents for references to outdoor dining, patio, or sidewalk cafe and found none.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-05 applies 'If outdoor dining in ROW' is proposed. The vision analysis and document review confirm no outdoor dining areas are proposed in the public right-of-way. The triggering condition is not met, so this checklist item does not apply to this project.
findings.explanation: No outdoor dining areas proposed in the ROW.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheets 14 and 15 identified an existing light pole in the ROW at the intersection of Collier Street and Evergreen Avenue (shown with the 'EXISTING LIGHT POLE' legend symbol). However, no proposed street lights or pedestrian lighting fixtures are labeled, called out, or shown in the ROW on these sheets or any other site plan sheets. Reviewed hardscape plan (Sheet 46) material schedule which lists 'STREET LIGHT' (Item 7.1) but vision analysis shows these are located on private property, not in the ROW. Reviewed general notes and found no License Agreement application or reference for pedestrian lighting in ROW.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-06 applies 'If pedestrian lighting in ROW' is proposed. The key word is 'proposed'—existing light poles do not trigger the License Agreement requirement. The vision analysis confirms that while existing lights are present in the ROW, no new/proposed pedestrian lighting is shown in the ROW. The street lights on the hardscape plan are on private property. The triggering condition for this checklist item is not met.
findings.explanation: No proposed pedestrian lighting shown in the ROW; only existing light poles present.

findings.observation: This is a catch-all item for any required License or Encroachment Agreement not covered by CC-24-01 through CC-24-06. Based on analysis of CC-24-04, street trees/landscaping are proposed in the Collier Street ROW (5' planting zone), which requires a License Agreement. Reviewed the Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 6) which explicitly states 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project? [ ] Yes (x) No'. Searched all supplementary documents and found no License Agreement or Encroachment Agreement applications. Searched site plan sheets for any references to License Agreements or Encroachment Agreements and found none. Sheet 6 shows AULCC requirement marked 'YES' but no License Agreement documentation is referenced.
findings.reasoning: The grouping overview states: 'All License and Encroachment Agreements must be approved or submitted prior to formal site plan approval—plans cannot receive formal approval without the required agreements in place.' The project clearly requires a License Agreement for street trees in ROW (per CC-24-04 analysis), yet none has been submitted or referenced on the plans. The Application affirmatively states NO License Agreement will be submitted, contradicting what is shown on the plans. This is a completeness deficiency—the required agreement is neither submitted as a supplementary document nor referenced on the plan sheets.
findings.explanation: License Agreement required for street trees in ROW but not submitted or referenced; Application states no License Agreement will be submitted despite plans showing ROW improvements requiring one.

evidenceLocations.label: Dimensional Control & Site Plan (ROW planting zone shown)
Consolidated Site Plan Application (License Agreement question marked 'No')

findings.resolution: Submit required License Agreement application for street trees and landscaping in Collier Street ROW, and reference the License Agreement on the site plans.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 18 (Overall Utility Plan) estimated approximately 80-110 linear feet of water and wastewater utility connections in the ROW, consisting of four perpendicular service taps in Collier Street (approximately 60-80 LF total) and one tap in S. Lamar Blvd (approximately 20-30 LF). All proposed utility mains/loops are located on private property; only short service connections extend into ROW to tie into existing mains. Reviewed facts.md which indicates the site is in 'Downtown Project Coordination Zone: South sector' but based on the site location at 1700 S. Lamar (south of Oltorf Street, which is the DAPCZ southern boundary per the grouping overview), the site appears to be outside the DAPCZ proper. The AULCC threshold for areas outside DAPCZ is 300 LF.
findings.reasoning: CC-24-15 triggers when excavations exceed 25 LF in DAPCZ or 300 LF outside DAPCZ. The estimated ROW utility work (80-110 LF) is well below the 300 LF threshold for non-DAPCZ areas. Even with conservative allowances, the total is definitively under 300 LF. Since the linear footage threshold is not exceeded, the condition 'If excavations exceed AULCC thresholds' is not met. This checklist item does not apply based on excavation length alone. (Note: CC-24-16 separately addresses AULCC triggered by License Agreements, regardless of excavation length.)
findings.explanation: ROW utility excavation work (~80-110 LF) is below the 300 LF AULCC threshold for areas outside DAPCZ.

findings.observation: Reviewed findings for CC-24-04 and CC-24-13, which confirm a License Agreement is required for street trees/landscaping in the Collier Street ROW. Per the grouping overview, AULCC coordination is triggered 'when a License Agreement or tower crane is involved' regardless of excavation length. Examined Sheet 6 (Austin Water General Information) which includes an 'AULCC REQUIREMENT' section. Vision tool analysis confirmed the 'YES' checkbox is marked, and the form states 'IF YES, PLEASE PROVIDE UCC# (pending)'. Searched entire project directory for AULCC case number, UCC number, or AULCC Completeness Letter—found only the 'pending' notation on Sheet 6. No actual AULCC case number or Completeness Letter is provided anywhere in the submittal. The grouping overview states: 'Case number and Completeness Letter must be in the submittal.'
findings.reasoning: The triggering condition 'If License Agreement or tower crane' is met—a License Agreement is required for street trees in ROW. When this condition is met, AULCC coordination documentation (case number and Completeness Letter) must be submitted. Sheet 6 acknowledges AULCC is required (checkbox marked YES) but provides no actual case number—only 'pending'. The grouping overview explicitly requires 'Case number and Completeness Letter must be in the submittal.' Marking a checkbox and noting 'pending' is not equivalent to submitting the required AULCC coordination documentation. The deficiency described in the checklist item—'Plans not submitted or referenced for AULCC when License Agreement or tower crane is involved'—is present.
findings.explanation: License Agreement required (for street trees in ROW), triggering AULCC coordination requirement. Sheet 6 acknowledges AULCC required but case number listed as 'pending'; no AULCC case number or Completeness Letter provided.

evidenceLocations.label: Austin Water General Information (AULCC checkbox marked YES, case number 'pending')

findings.resolution: Submit plans to AULCC for coordination and provide the AULCC case number and Completeness Letter in the site plan submittal. Reference the AULCC case number on Sheet 6 where currently listed as 'pending'.
